hero.heading: M&M Body Shop, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built October 4, 2026, from mandmbodyshop.com, the industry's billing survey, and federal data. Every number is labeled: published, federal, or our assumption. The assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: (exact: $3,361 and $37,842) Under $5,000 a figure rounds to the nearest $1,000, above it to the nearest $5,000; the exact figures govern.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Repairs you complete in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per hundred repairs.

sliders.label: Repairs that need a second estimate after teardown
Cost of one second estimate, in days, paperwork, and rental
Manufacturer-required operations per repair
sliders.basis: Scans, calibrations, one-time-use parts, and procedure steps. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Required operations performed and never paid
Months between estimate and parts order
sliders.basis: Half a month to two months, about two to eight weeks. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

constants.text: Federal series: BLS producer price index, motor vehicle parts (WPU1412), 145.456 in October 2025 to 149.359 in August 2026, its latest published month: up 2.7 percent over ten months, 0.27 percent per month [[BENCHMARK]]. The model applies it only across the weeks between estimate and parts order. Next release October 15, 2026; this page changes with it.

terms.label: Required operations performed and never paid
Parts drift between estimate and order

model.formulaText: Moved per 100 repairs = 100 × second-estimate share × cost per second estimate + 100 × required operations per repair × value per operation × unpaid share + 100 × parts per repair × months of lag × (149.359 ÷ 145.456 minus 1) ÷ 10
model.plainText: In words, the second estimates written once a vehicle is apart, at their cost in days and paperwork, plus the manufacturer-required operations performed and never paid, plus what parts prices add while an estimate waits for its parts order.
model.callout: What nobody counts is what the certifications cost to keep. A certified repair means scans, calibrations, one-time-use parts, and the manufacturer's procedure, whether or not the first estimate saw them. Nobody counts how many of your repairs needed a second estimate once the vehicle was apart, what each cost in days and rental, or how many required operations were performed and never paid. The industry's own survey of 473 shops says insurers pay most of the time when a documented line is on the estimate; shops that never ask lose.

smallRound.note: Under $5,000, a figure rounds to the nearest $1,000.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: You and your family built the shop from the ground up in 1983 and kept earning what most shops never attempt: certification by Ford, by General Motors, by Honda and Acura, and I-CAR Gold Class [[OBSERVED]].
Voted the county's best body shop six years running. A lifetime warranty on your craftsmanship [[OBSERVED]].
A line on your site that explains the rest: you follow the manufacturer's procedures so a vehicle's safety systems come back restored and recalibrated [[OBSERVED]].

proposal.heading: What we propose
proposal.lead: The proposal: the count (first estimate against final, supplements by cause, required operations performed against paid), the repair plan after teardown with the manufacturer's procedure attached to every required line, and the thirty-day result; fixed fee between $1,500 and $2,500; read-only; no customer or vehicle identity leaves the building.

ledger.title: What one repair's second estimate looks like
ledger.label: Illustrative, not M&M Body Shop data
ledger.note: In the repair plan, every required line carries the manufacturer's procedure before the estimate leaves. Every line and figure is invented to show the format.

proposal.promise: If your records show our printed range overstated your exposure, our findings letter says so in those words.
